corrected_value.authors: Derwing, T. M., & Munro, M. J.
corrected_value.title: Accent, intelligibility, and comprehensibility: Evidence from four L1s.

decisions.quote: Abstract This study investigated the relationship among intelligibility, comprehensibility, and accentedness in the speech of second language learners of Spanish of varying proficiency in instructed contexts. It conceptually replicated studies by Munro and Derwing (1995a) and Derwing and Munro (1997), who found partial independence among the three speech dimensions but also evidence that proficiency may mediate the relationship between linguistic features of stimuli (e.g., phonemic and grammatical error rates) and speech dimensions.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The abstract explicitly states that the study conceptually replicated both Munro and Derwing (1995a) and Derwing and Munro (1997), specifically retesting their findings of partial independence among intelligibility, comprehensibility, and accentedness and proficiency mediation of the relationship between linguistic error rates and speech dimensions using new speech data from 42 L2 Spanish learners rated by 80 native Spanish listeners. The supplied publisher reference list provides the full bibliographic identity for Derwing and Munro (1997) in Studies in Second Language Acquisition (19, 1-16, DOI 10.1017/S0272263197001010), confirmed in Crossref metadata. Shipped row 1267 (Munro & Derwing, 1995, Language Learning, 45, 73-97, DOI 10.1111/j.1467-1770.1995.tb00963.x) matches sibling target_index 0; Derwing and Munro (1997) is a separate subsequent empirical study across four L1s rather than an alternate report of the 1995 paper, and is genuinely absent from the shipped rows.
